chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about the man and the woman, is it permissible for them to insert medication while they insert medication while they are fasting? He said: There is no problem.
ai.seo_question: Does inserting medication break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), the concept of 'istadkhal' (introducing medicine) is clarified to include injections and other forms of internal delivery, distinguishing them from eating and drinking. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it demonstrates that the breaking of the fast requires the consumption of substantial matter through the natural orifice, whereas injections do not constitute a nullifier, thereby preserving the validity of the fast for the sick or those requiring treatment.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man and the woman, is it correct for them that the medication is inserted into them and they are both Fasting?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-‘Amrakiy ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja’far from his brother who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man and woman who apply medicine inside.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
